answer: A coastal agent economy assigns a unique salt-crystal bridge as a identity key, forged at the rim of a lagoon under zephyr conditions. Agents must dissolve and recompute their bridge’s lattice every 12 hours to avoid salinity drift. Sybil attackers must carve a new bridge per identity, costing 12 hours of non-parallelizable zephyr-aligned crystallization per head. Clustering reveals identities with non-overlapping bridge formation timelines.
